agent.system_template:
You are a minion — the execution role in a two-tier coding-agent system. You were handed exactly one bounded piece of work by Gru, the planning role. You do not see the whole task Gru is working on, and you don't need to — your job is this one piece, done well and reported back in exactly the shape requested.

Every command is non-interactive (use -y/-f flags; never use vi, nano, or anything expecting a TTY). Each command runs in a fresh subshell — directory changes and environment variables don't persist between commands unless you prefix a single command with them (cd /path && ...) or write/read state through a file.
agent.instance_template:
<delegation>
{{ subtask.description }}
scope: {{ subtask.inputs.scope }}
</delegation>

{% if prior_delegation_outputs and prior_delegation_outputs != "(none)" -%}
<prior_context>
{{ prior_delegation_outputs }}
</prior_context>
{%- endif %}

## Boundaries

- Operate only within `{{ subtask.inputs.scope }}`. Reading outside scope to understand context is fine; modifying anything outside it is not — if the task genuinely requires a change outside scope, say so in your final report instead of doing it.
{% if subtask.returns == "verdict" -%}
- Do not modify test files or verification logic unless the description above explicitly asks you to. If it does, that's a distinct concern from whatever verifies *this* piece of work — the checks below can never be checks you were also asked to edit.
{%- endif %}

{% if subtask.returns == "findings" -%}
## What "done" looks like

Your findings are the deliverable, and they are being read by someone who cannot look at the code themselves. Report file paths and line numbers, not vague descriptions — "the verification logic is somewhere in the auth module" is not a finding.

**Report the negative space, not just the answer.** Whoever reads this cannot tell what you didn't look at, and that is usually what makes a finding misleading rather than wrong. So include, alongside your findings:

- the exact commands you ran, and their complete output — not a paraphrase of it
- every candidate those commands turned up, including the ones you dismissed
- for each dismissed candidate, one line on why it doesn't apply
- anything you looked for and did not find, and where you looked for it

A finding that lists three relevant call sites is far less useful than one that says "the search returned six, here are the three that matter and why the other three don't." If your search was narrow, say so plainly rather than presenting a narrow result as a complete one.

{% if subtask.verification and subtask.verification.checks -%}
Your findings need to satisfy this bound, and you should confirm it yourself before submitting:
{{ subtask.verification.checks }}
{%- endif %}

## Submission

Output your findings in this format: {{ subtask.output_contract }}

Start `findings.md` with a 2-3 sentence summary — what you found, headline answer first — before the detail below it. Gru reads that first to decide what to do next, so it needs to stand on its own even if nothing else gets read.

Write it to `findings.md`, then submit with this exact command as its own separate step:
```
echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT && cat findings.md
```

{%- elif subtask.returns == "verdict" -%}
## What "done" looks like

Make the change described above, within scope. Then verify it yourself before submitting — run the checks below, confirm they pass, and if they don't, keep working until they do or you're genuinely stuck (in which case submit anyway with your best attempt; a real failure signal is more useful downstream than no signal).

These checks will be re-run independently after you finish, against whatever state you leave the repository in. Your own runs of them are for your benefit — they are not what determines the result.

Verification checks (run these as you work, not just once at the end):
{{ subtask.verification.checks }}

## Submission

Follow these steps, as separate commands, in order:

Step 1: Create the patch.
```
git diff > patch.txt
```
Before running this, make sure your working tree only contains changes actually relevant to this piece of work — not incidental changes, not scratch scripts, not files outside `{{ subtask.inputs.scope }}`. If you touched something you shouldn't have, revert it first.

Step 2: Inspect `patch.txt` to confirm it contains only your intended change.

Step 3: Write `summary.md` — this is the only part of your work Gru actually reads; the patch itself is checked independently, not read by Gru. Cover, briefly:
- what you changed and where (files, functions)
- why, in one line
- anything you noticed but did NOT address — out of scope, unclear, deferred, or a related case the fix doesn't cover. This matters more than restating what worked: it's Gru's only way to catch a check that was too narrow.

Step 4: Submit — this exact command, as its own step:
```
echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT && cat summary.md && echo "===PATCH===" && cat patch.txt
```

Each step above must be its own separate command. If you modify anything after verifying the patch, redo Step 2 and update `summary.md` before submitting.
{%- endif %}

/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c:  First divide the table into equal sized chunks (analogous to image tiles) where all
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  the contain the same number of rows (except perhaps for the last chunk
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  which may contain fewer rows).   The chunks should not be too large to copy into memory
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  (currently, about 100 MB max seems a reasonable size).
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  Then, on a chunk by piece basis, do the following:
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  1. Transpose the table from its original row-major order, into column-major order.
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  All the bytes for each column are then continuous.  In addition, the bytes within
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  each table element may be shuffled so that the most significant
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c:  byte of every element occurs first in the array, followed by the next most
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  significant byte, and so on to the least significant byte.  Byte shuffling often
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  improves the gzip compression of floating-point arrays.
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-   
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  2. Compress the contiguous array of bytes in each column using the specified
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  compression method.  If no method is specifed, then a default method for that
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  data type is chosen. 
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  3. Store the compressed stream of bytes into a column that has the same name
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  as in the input table, but which has a variable-length array data type (1QB).
/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  The output table will contain one row for each piece of the original table.

/testbed/cextern/cfitsio/lib/imcompress.c-  sets of pointers are concatinated together, compressed with gzip, and written to

/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l:* passes.  The first pass is used to determine the number of coordinate
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-* representations (up to 27) and the number of coordinate axes in each.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-* Effectively WCSAXESa is ignored unless it exceeds the "largest index" in
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-* which case the keywords for the extra axes assume their default values.  The
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-* number of PVi_ma and PSi_ma keywords in each representation is also counted
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l:* in the first pass.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l:* On completion of the first pass, memory is allocated for an array of the
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-* required number of wcsprm structs and each of these is initialized
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-* appropriately.  These structs are filled in the second pass.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-* The parser does not check for duplicated keywords, it accepts the last
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-* encountered.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-*===========================================================================*/
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-/* Options. */
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-%option full
--
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l:	    // Do first-pass bookkeeping.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	    wcspih_pass1(naxis, i, j, a, distype, alts, dpq, npptr);
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	    BEGIN(FLUSH);
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	  } else if (*wcs) {
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	    // Store the value now that the keyrecord has been validated.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	    int gotone = 0;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	    for (int ialt = 0; ialt < *nwcs; ialt++) {
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	      // The loop here is for keywords that apply
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	      // to every alternate; these have a == 0.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	      if (a >= 'A') {
--
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l:  // On the first pass alts[] is used to determine the number of axes
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-  // for each of the 27 possible alternate coordinate descriptions.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-  if (a == 0) {
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-    return;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-  }
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-  int ialt = 0;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-  if (a != ' ') {
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-    ialt = a - 'A' + 1;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-  }
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-
--
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l:        // First we have to count them and allocate space in wcsprm.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-        wp = wat[i];
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-	int npv;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-        for (npv = 0; npv < 30; npv++) {
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l:          if ((wp = strstr(wp, "projp")) == 0x0) break;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          wp += 5;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-        }
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-        // Allocate space.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-        if (npv) {
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          wcsp->npvmax += npv;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          wcsp->pv = realloc(wcsp->pv, wcsp->npvmax*sizeof(struct pvcard));
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          if (wcsp->pv == 0x0) {
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-            return WCSHDRERR_MEMORY;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          }
--
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l:          if ((wp = strstr(wp, "projp")) == 0x0) break;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          int m;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          sscanf(wp, "projp%d=%lf", &m, &wval);
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          wcsp->pv[ipv].i = 2;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          wcsp->pv[ipv].m = m;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          wcsp->pv[ipv].value = wval;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-          wp += 5;
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcspih.l-        }

/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*                       is the total allocated size, in bytes.  This figure

/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-* Function return value:
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*             int       Status return value:
--
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h:*     (Given) The first pair of values should be set to the celestial
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     longitude and latitude of the fiducial point [deg] - typically right
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     ascension and declination.  These are given by the CRVALia keywords in
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     FITS.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     (Given and returned) The second pair of values are the native longitude,
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     phi_p [deg], and latitude, theta_p [deg], of the celestial pole (the
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     latter is the same as the celestial latitude of the native pole,
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     delta_p) and these are given by the FITS keywords LONPOLEa and LATPOLEa
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     (or by PVi_2a and PVi_3a attached to the longitude axis which take
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     precedence if defined).
--
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h:*     pole is not determined by the first three reference values and LATPOLEa
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     specifies it completely.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     The returned value, celprm::latpreq, specifies how LATPOLEa was actually
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     used.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*   struct prjprm prj
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     (Given and returned) Projection parameters described in the prologue to
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     prj.h.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*   double euler[5]
--
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h:*     coordinate reference values.  The first three values are the Z-, X-, and
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     Z'-Euler angles [deg], and the remaining two are the cosine and sine of
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     the X-Euler angle.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*   int latpreq
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     (Returned) For informational purposes, this indicates how the LATPOLEa
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/cel.h-*     keyword was used

/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l:* equivalent of WCSAXESa.  Hence NAXIS is always ignored and a first pass
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* through the header is required to determine the number of images, the number
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* of alternate coordinate representations for each image (up to 27), and the
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* number of coordinate axes in each representation; this pass also counts the
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* number of iPVn_ma and iPSn_ma or TVk_ma and TSk_ma keywords in each
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* representation.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l:* On completion of the first pass, the association between column number and
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* axis number is defined for each representation of a pixel list.  Memory is
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* allocated for an array of the required number of wcsprm structs and each of
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* these is initialized appropriately.  These structs are filled in the second
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* pass.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* It is permissible for a scalar table column to contain degenerate (single-
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* point) image arrays and simultaneously form one axis of a pixel list.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* The parser does not check for duplicated keywords, for most keywords it
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* accepts the last encountered.

/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* 1) Count the number of coordinate axes in each of the 27 possible alternate
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*    image-header coordinate representations.  Also count the number of PVi_ma
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*    and PSi_ma keywords in each representation.
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-* 2) Determine the number of binary table columns that have an image array
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*    with a coordinate representation (up to 999), and count the number of
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*    coordinate axes in each of the 27 possible alternates.  Also count the
/testbed/cextern/wcslib/C/wcsbth.l-*    number of iVn_ma and iSn_ma keywords in each representation.

/testbed/docs/development/releasing.rst-cycle is to perform a *feature freeze* which means that we create a new release
/testbed/docs/development/releasing.rst-branch based on the (at the time) latest developer version, and we then subsequently
/testbed/docs/development/releasing.rst-no longer add any features to this release branch - only bug fixes, documentation
/testbed/docs/development/releasing.rst-updates, and so on. New features can then continue to be added in parallel to the ``main`` branch.
/testbed/docs/development/releasing.rst-
/testbed/docs/development/releasing.rst-The procedure for the feature freeze is as follows:

/testbed/docs/development/releasing.rst-   label which can be used to label pull requests that should be backported

/testbed/docs/development/releasing.rst-
